items.title: Supervisory guidance: digital-asset client onboarding and custody
items.text:
Dear Mr. Bell,

The examination team of the Office of Financial Supervision writes to draw your attention to interim guidance recently issued by this Office on the onboarding and servicing of clients whose wealth derives, in whole or in material part, from digital assets.

The interim guidance sets out the Office's expectations for regulated institutions in three areas.

First, anti-money laundering controls. Transaction monitoring should be able to trace relevant on-chain flows, including the provenance of assets before conversion to fiat. Institutions should be able to identify exposure to mixers, sanctioned addresses and high-risk exchanges.

Second, custody due diligence. Where client assets are held with, or flow through, third-party digital-asset custodians, the institution should document its due diligence on those custodians. This includes their control environment, segregation of client assets and regulatory standing.

Third, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification. Verification should be supported by evidence that an examiner can independently review, not by client attestation alone.

Given Halcyon Ridge Capital's wealth management and lending activities, we ask that the firm submit a written risk assessment by August 29, 2026. The assessment should address:
- the firm's current and prospective exposure to digital-asset-derived clients;
- the adequacy of existing AML, KYC and sanctions screening controls against the expectations above;
- any remediation planned, with timelines.

Final guidance is expected later this year. The Office may take your response into account in scoping the firm's next examination.

Please direct questions to the examination team at this address.

Sincerely,

Examination Division
Office of Financial Supervision

items.title: Assess digital-asset client onboarding risk (OFS guidance)
items.text:
On Jul 28, the Office of Financial Supervision sent us a letter (cc Catherine) about its interim guidance on onboarding clients with digital-asset-derived wealth. OFS expects three things:
- AML controls that can trace on-chain flows
- documented due diligence on crypto custodians
- source-of-funds verification that holds up to examiner review

OFS wants a written risk assessment by 2026-08-29.

Nadia, please assess the following:
1. Whether AMLMonitor, FraudScore and SanctionsScreen can meet the on-chain tracing expectation today.
2. What blockchain analytics tooling or vendors we have, if any.
3. Our current exposure: how many wealth prospects and clients have crypto-derived wealth.
4. Your recommendation on whether we keep onboarding these clients while gaps exist.

I'd like findings in hand before the #crypto-policy working group gets going. I'll draft the OFS response from this ticket.

--- Comment by Nadia Petrov ---
Initial findings on controls.

AMLMonitor cannot trace on-chain flows. It monitors fiat activity sourced from DataLake and scored by FraudScore. It has no wallet or address data model and no ingestion of blockchain data. When a client wires in proceeds from an exchange, all we see is the wire from the exchange's bank. Anything upstream of that is invisible to us.

SanctionsScreen screens names and entities against OFAC and other lists. It does not screen wallet addresses, even though OFAC publishes those on the SDN list.

We have no blockchain analytics vendor in place. There is no contract and no pilot. Procurement has no record of an evaluation either.

Today, source of funds for these clients rests on two things: exchange statements and client-provided wallet screenshots. Both are documents we cannot independently verify.

--- Comment by Nadia Petrov ---
Exposure. I worked through ClientHub notes and KYCPipeline cases with the Wealth Management client associates. There are 9 current wealth prospects whose wealth is substantially crypto-derived: early holders, token-project founders, and a couple of mining-related liquidity events. None are fully onboarded yet. Several are sitting in EDD review in KYCPipeline.

Custody: at least four of the 9 hold assets with third-party crypto custodians. We have done no due diligence on any of those custodians.

--- Comment by Nadia Petrov ---
My recommendation is to pause new digital-asset client onboarding until both of these are true:
(a) a blockchain analytics tool is integrated into AMLMonitor, with alerting on wallet risk and address screening wired into SanctionsScreen;
(b) OFS publishes its final guidance.

Enhanced due diligence on its own does not close the gap. Without on-chain visibility we cannot evidence source of funds, and that is exactly what OFS says examiners will test.

For the 9 prospects, I suggest we hold the KYCPipeline cases in their current state rather than decline outright. Relationship managers can then tell clients the delay is a process matter.

Marking this resolved from the assessment side. Implementing any pause is a policy decision for the working group.

--- Comment by Marcus Bell ---
Thanks Nadia, this is what I needed. I'll use these findings for the OFS risk assessment and take the pause recommendation to #crypto-policy. Resolving.

I want to make the case for continuing before we lock in a pause. We have 14 prospects in the pipeline, roughly $40M of AUM, and our competitors are onboarding these exact clients right now. I think an enhanced due diligence package could get us there in the meantime: exchange statements, independent tax-return review and third-party attestations.

Grace, I hear you on the pipeline, but COMP-112 is pretty clear: AMLMonitor can't see on-chain flows, and we have no analytics vendor. EDD on paper doesn't change that. If OFS asks us to evidence source of funds, we can't, and their Jul 28 letter says that's exactly what they'll test.

Adding the risk side: even with clean source of funds, we'd be relying on crypto custodians we've done zero diligence on. That's real counterparty and custody exposure, especially if any of these relationships turn into lending collateral. Before we say yes, I'd want to know the exit plan. If final guidance tightens after we've onboarded, how do we offboard or de-risk those clients without trapping assets?

Catching up on this thread. $40M of AUM is meaningful, but it's not worth a regulatory finding while OFS has us in scope and we owe them a risk assessment by Aug 29. Both sides have made a fair case, so I'd suggest we take it to the board risk committee on Aug 21 and let them make the call. Marcus and Grace, can you each bring a one-pager?
